Security & Accountability

Blink Discloses Admin Tool Breach, Reimburses Users, and Offers 50% Bounty on Stolen Bitcoin

An attacker leveraged stacked permission flaws in inherited support software to drain 6.61 BTC from 24 accounts; Blink contained the breach in fifteen minutes, restored balances from shareholder reserves, and set a 3.3 BTC bounty for fund recovery and circular economies.

By The Observer Dispatch Desk · Sourced from Blink Wallet

In an exhaustive and unusually direct post-mortem published this weekend, custodial wallet provider Blink disclosed a September 19 attack in which an intruder exploited a vulnerability in support administration software to take control of 35 accounts and siphon 6.61 BTC from 24 of them. Within fifteen minutes of a customer alerting engineers at 11:39 UTC, Blink shut down its custodial service entirely. By that evening the security flaw had been patched and the platform reopened. Five days later, all affected customer accounts had been replenished to the satoshi with shareholder capital, ensuring No customer bears any loss.

The post-mortem made no attempt to deflect responsibility onto third-party infrastructure or users. This was our fault. Not Bitcoin's, not our users'. The vulnerability dated back to October 2023, residing in inherited administrative tools where three permission-checking oversights cascaded together. A user with a basic account could escalate privileges through a web browser, modify account emails or phone numbers, and raise withdrawal thresholds. The team had been heavily engaged in migrating tens of thousands of users toward self-custodial accounts under new regulatory mandates, leaving internal administrative anomalies undetected by monitors geared toward network outages.

While the attacker accessed metadata for 3,817 accounts—primarily phone numbers and email addresses—core cold-storage reserves and non-custodial accounts remained completely untouched. What proved decisive in preventing total drainage was two-factor authentication. Nine accounts targeted by the intruder had 2FA activated; across eighteen attempts to initiate transfers, the attacker was stopped dead with zero loss. By contrast, every one of the 24 drained accounts had two-factor authentication disabled.

Rather than quietly write off the missing funds, Blink announced a 50% recovery bounty—up to 3.3 BTC. Informants providing actionable intelligence that leads to fund recovery will receive 25% of retrieved coins, while another 25% is pledged directly to grassroots circular economies, including Bitcoin Beach in El Salvador, Bitcoin Ekasi in South Africa, and Afribit Kibera in Kenya. As Blink noted, We would far rather have spent this money on grassroots Bitcoin adoption than lost it to a thief.

Relay Infrastructure

Operators Fortify Relays with Go-Python Write Policies Against Persistent Botnet Probes

Sourced from someone

Relay infrastructure operator someone provided an operational briefing detailing active countermeasures against a sustained wave of automated traffic targeting Nostr hubs. Relay operators report that 2450+ bots banned. attacks are continuing. with millions of compromised edge devices participating in coordinated request floods designed to overwhelm storage backends.

In response, major public relay nos.lol transitioned its ingestion engine to a hybrid architecture: nos.lol is now also new paradigm (go+python) write policy. expect faster writes. stable reads. Parallel efforts at nostr.mom have restored automated kind 1984 moderation reporting, using local language model passes to isolate spam vectors while node operators compile a cross-relay IP reputation catalog to preserve open relay availability.

Freedom Tech Perspectives

Desktop Linux Finds New Life as the Natural Substrate for AI Agents

Sourced from Ungovernable

Reflecting on twenty years of desktop workstation management on Freedom Tech Friday, Nathan Day argued that traditional operating system complaints have flipped into systemic advantages: What used to be its Achilles heel, which is a load of text based config files and CLIs, has now, in an agentic age, become its superpower, because agents can just drive Linux. Where graphical desktop operating systems isolate automation behind brittle interfaces, terminal-native architectures offer agents direct, programmatic leverage.

Hardware, Sovereign Systems & Protocol Frontiers

Air-gapped Keys, Inscriptionless Media, and Physical Coercion Defenses
Air-Gapped Signers

Savepoint Signer: Cold Storage Disguised in a Game Boy Color

Sourced from Librería de Satoshi

At the Madrid BitDevs technical salon hosted alongside Watch Out, Bitcoin!, developer Alvaro Roble demonstrated a functional hardware signer built entirely within a vintage Nintendo Game Boy Color. Termed Savepoint Signer, un firmante de PSBTs escondido dentro de una Game Boy Color. Experimental, solo para fondos de prueba pero una gran joya cypherpunk, the device transforms eight-bit gaming hardware into an air-gapped cryptographic signing computer, parsing Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions via camera and display.

Media Publishing

BPUB Protocol Embeds Media into Script Witnesses Without Envelopes

Sourced from Hampus

Developer Hampus released an update to BcashJr Wallet introducing media publishing support over the BIP110/Blake chain using the BPUB protocol. Unlike standard Ordinals techniques, BPUB doesn’t use Ordinals inscription envelopes. It embeds file data into public keys within multisig scripts, then reveals those scripts in transaction witnesses.

Discussing the engineering process, Hampus noted: It's fully vibecoded, with ChatGPT 5.3 Sol and then later 6 Astra. However, I’ve been building Bitcoin wallets for years, so I brought that experience to it. Also ran a code review with Kimi 3. Citing developer reflections, the implementation relies on script reveal mechanisms to bypass filtering.

Custody Architecture

Miniscript Time-Locks Designed to Neutralize Physical Coercion

Sourced from wave.space 🇪🇺

Responding to growing anxieties surrounding physical extortion and home invasions, self-custody platform wave.space rolled out collaborative vaults constructed with Miniscript. Two keys reside on air-gapped hardware authenticators signing by optical QR code, while a third co-signing key acts as an administrative sentinel that cannot move funds independently.

The architecture targets extortion directly: all unassisted withdrawals enforce a strict 365-day consensus lock that no physical duress can shorten, while standard transactions trigger instantaneous broadcast alerts, providing a time window to cancel unauthorized transfers before funds settle.

Prison Bureaucracy

Transfer Furlough Denied for Keonne Rodriguez Without Explanation

Sourced from Ungovernable

In Letter 7 of Notes from the Inside, advocates for Samourai Wallet co-founder Keonne Rodriguez reported that his application for a transfer furlough was summarily rejected by the Bureau of Prisons. Classified as minimum security with two years of compliant pretrial release, self-surrender, and zero disciplinary marks, Rodriguez requested permission to drive himself to his designated facility at his own expense. Three days later the request was denied without explanation, routing him through federal transit estimated to cost taxpayers $10,000.
